Six Lines: Cast and Lay Out the Chart

The Six Lines method gives every line of a hexagram a branch, an element and a family role, then reads them against the month and day of the cast. This page lays out the chart exactly as the 1690 handbook 增刪卜易 does, and shows where each fact comes from.

Moment of the cast

· The month (月建) turns at the solar term and the day (日辰) at 23:00, as in the classical calendar. The moment is set to now when the page opens.

The coin throws and the chart are worked out on this device. Nothing is sent to us.

How the chart is built, in the book's words

Branches for each trigram, inner and outer:

「乾在內：子水寅木辰土。乾在外：午火申金戌土。」

Family roles by the palace element:

「乾兌宮金兄、土父、木財、火鬼、水子。」

應 sits two lines away from 世:

「隔世爻兩位卽是應爻」

Quoted from 增刪卜易 (1690), public domain.

What is the question about?

Traditional text

For each kind of question the book reads one line, the 用神. Pick one to see which line that is and what the month and day do to it. Health questions are not covered here.

「月建能生克沖合」 「日辰能生克沖合」

These are the facts the book reads from. Fate Tutor does not turn them into a forecast.

Reading the chart

世 is the line for you, the one asking; 應 is the other side.

The five relatives: 兄弟 siblings and friends · 父母 parents, documents, home · 子孫 offspring and ease · 官鬼 office and pressure · 妻財 money and goods.

A moving line changes into a new line; its family role is still counted from the original palace: 「六親須照前卦」

If a relative is on no line, the book looks for it in the palace's first hexagram, hidden under the same line: 「則本宮首卦尋之」

The six spirits start from the day stem and count upward. The book warns against reading them on their own: 「須以用神爲主」

「甲子旬中戌亥空」 · 「月建沖之爲月破」

Where this comes from

增刪卜易, 火珠林 and 京氏易傳

The chart rules come from 增刪卜易 (野鶴老人, 1690). The order of the eight palaces and the stems come from 京氏易傳 (Jing Fang, Han dynasty), and 火珠林 confirms the order of the six spirits. All three are public domain on Chinese Wikisource.

Checked line by line: the engine reproduces all 64 hexagrams of the book's chart and its worked examples. The online copy has a few copying slips, such as 士 for 土; our checker names each one. The book's two 六神 examples swap 勾陳 and 螣蛇 against its own table; this page follows the table, which 火珠林 agrees with.

About this tradition

A chart of the moment, read line by line

Six Lines (六爻, also called 納甲 or 火珠林 method) grew from Jing Fang's Han-dynasty system. Instead of reading the I Ching's words, it reads the elements and family roles of each line against the month and day.

Fate Tutor lays out the chart and shows its sources. It does not turn a cast into a forecast, financial advice, medical advice or a decision made for you.

These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
